name: Marshall Islands
headline: A 2025 data law covering only government bodies gives no record access right and is not yet in force, while most records stay on paper.

access.summary: No law giving patients a right to see or copy their health record was found, and there is no patient portal. The 2025 data protection law covers only government bodies, has no access right and takes effect 12 months after its 7 October 2025 certification.
detail: Section 13 of the Constitution protects people from unreasonable intrusions into their privacy. It does not give a right to obtain records.

The Personal Data Protection Act 2025 applies only to core government ministries and agencies. Its six principles include accuracy, and a court may order a ministry to correct or delete inaccurate data. The Act contains no right for a person to see or get a copy of their data.
Section 117 says the Act takes effect 12 months after certification. The Speaker certified it on 7 October 2025, so it was not yet in force on 1 October 2026.
No patient portal was found. We could not open the full Revised Code, so the absence of any record-access rule elsewhere is not verified. Score sits in the lower half of the 15 to 35 band.

sources.title: Personal Data Protection Act 2025 (P.L. 2025-43), Nitijela
Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI Judiciary copy)

control.summary: No opt-out, granular choice or patient-visible access log was found. Only sexually transmitted disease information has a statutory consent rule, and the 2025 law lets ministries share personal data with each other without asking the person.
detail: Section 1506 of the Communicable Diseases Prevention and Control Act 1988 keeps information on people tested for or infected with an STD, including HIV, confidential. It may be released with the person's consent, to their physician, in an emergency, to a spouse of a person with HIV, and to blood banks, schools and prisons.
The Cancer Registry Act 2009 requires every cancer diagnosed or treated in the country to be registered. It contains no patient consent or opt-out.

Section 115 of the Personal Data Protection Act 2025 lets core ministries share personal data among themselves under a safe harbor if the sharing serves a legitimate function. No consent is required. This places the Marshall Islands in the 20 to 35 band.

privacy.summary: Health data is protected mainly by narrow sector laws, such as a $1,000 fine for leaking STD information and a $2,000 fine for Health Fund staff disclosures. The 2025 data protection law is not yet in force, and its staff were unfunded and unappointed in March 2026.
detail: The Personal Data Protection Act 2025 names health data as sensitive personal data. It binds only core government bodies, excludes law enforcement and national security, sets no breach notification duty and bars courts from awarding damages against a ministry.

The Economic Policy, Planning and Statistics Office is the competent authority. A World Bank mission in March 2026 reported it was awaiting government funding and appointment of data protection staff.

Sector rules: release of STD information in breach of the 1988 Act carries a $1,000 civil fine per offense. Health Fund staff who disclose a covered person's information face up to one year in prison, a $2,000 fine, or both.
No major health data breach was verified. The Marshall Islands is not in the EU, so GDPR and the EHDS do not apply.

commercial.summary: No law limits the sale of health data, its use in marketing, data brokers or health apps. The 2025 data protection law binds only core government bodies, so private clinics, insurers and app makers fall outside it.
detail: Section 103 of the Personal Data Protection Act 2025 limits it to core government ministries and agencies. Section 105 excludes state-owned enterprises from that definition.
No rule on selling health data, marketing use or de-identified data sales was found in the laws we opened.
Levellers.ai, a consultancy, says the Act does not on its face regulate the private sector. That matches the text.

sources.title: Personal Data Protection Act 2025 (P.L. 2025-43), Nitijela
AI Regulation in the Marshall Islands (Levellers.ai)

journey.summary: Records are mostly on paper outside the hospitals. A 2025 study found an electronic record in 1 of 60 facilities (1.7%), and a 2023 World Bank review found no system to track primary care patients over time.
detail: The JMIR study counted 60 health facilities and found an electronic health record in 1 (1.7%). It cites a Ministry hospital information system (mHIS) supplied by Advmeds. Which hospital uses it was not verified.
The World Bank primary care review says clinics record basic patient information on charts and enter diabetes measures in spreadsheets, with no system to track care longitudinally.
The Ministry runs an online Marshall Islands Immunization Registry on WebIZ, and the Cancer Registry Act 2009 creates a national cancer registry.
A World Bank-funded project plans Starlink internet for 34 health centers, with contracts expected in August 2026.

clinical.summary: A clinician outside the main hospital usually works from paper. Only 1 of 60 facilities had an electronic record in a 2025 study, so a cross-provider view of a patient's history is not available at national scale.
detail: The World Bank review found that primary care clinics record basic patient information on charts, which help them refer patients to hospitals. It found no system for tracking a patient's care over time.
The JMIR study found an electronic record in 1 of 60 facilities. A shared record linking the Majuro and Ebeye hospitals with outer island dispensaries was not found.
The STD law allows release of confidential information to medical personnel in a medical emergency.

research.summary: The Ministry's Institutional Review Committee must approve release of confidential cancer registry data for research, and registry data is confidential by law. There is no consent or opt-out rule for research use of other health records.
detail: The Cancer Registry Act 2009 makes reported information confidential and privileged, usable only for the study. Before releasing confidential data to researchers or other registries, the Secretary must have approval from the Ministry's Institutional Review Committee or an equivalent human subjects committee.
The STD law allows release only in a form that identifies no one for statistical purposes.
No general consent, opt-out or public register for secondary use was found. Clinical trial consent rules were not verified. Base 40, plus 3 for the ethics body and 3 for statutory confidentiality.

sources.title: Cancer Registry Act 2009, Nitijela

ai.summary: No law, guidance or device rule for clinical AI was found. A June 2026 review says the country has no AI law, bill, strategy or regulator, and none of its 2025 digital laws mentions AI.
detail: Levellers.ai, a consultancy, reports no AI law, AI regulator, risk-tiering or impact assessment duty. It says the 2025 data protection, cybersecurity and cybercrime laws do not mention AI.
No medical device regulation covering AI software was found. The Pacific Basin Telehealth Resource Center reports no telehealth laws in the country.
With nothing verified from an official source, the Marshall Islands falls in the 15 to 30 band for non-EU countries.

journeyNote: Primary care runs on charts. One facility had an electronic record in 2024 data. Immunization has an online WebIZ registry and cancer has a national registry. The Health Fund may hire claims administrators; links to clinical records were not verified.

laws.name: Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Article II section 13
laws.what: Freedom from unreasonable interference in personal choices and from unreasonable intrusions into privacy.

laws.name: Personal Data Protection Act 2025 (P.L. 2025-43)
laws.what: Data principles for core government bodies only; health data sensitive; no access right; no damages; effective 12 months after certification.

laws.name: Communicable Diseases Prevention and Control Act 1988, 7 MIRC Ch.15
laws.what: STD and HIV information confidential; release with consent or listed exceptions; $1,000 fine per breach.

laws.name: Cancer Registry Act 2009
laws.what: Mandatory national cancer registry; data confidential; research release needs Institutional Review Committee approval.

laws.name: Marshall Islands Health Fund Act of 2002, 7 MIRC Ch.2
laws.what: Health Fund for covered persons; staff disclosure of personal information is an offense, up to $2,000 fine.

laws.name: Digital Transformation and Identity Verification Act 2025
laws.what: Digital identity system; section 118 applies data protection principles and security duties to participating public bodies.

news.headline: Speaker certifies Personal Data Protection Act covering government ministries only
news.why: First data protection law, but patients get no access right and private providers are outside it.

news.headline: Review finds no AI law, strategy or regulator in the Marshall Islands
news.why: AI tools used in care face no national rules on safety or oversight.

news.headline: World Bank says data protection office still awaits funding and staff
news.why: Without staff, the new law's complaints and guidance duties cannot start.

news.headline: UN rapporteur urges access to nuclear testing archives and medical studies
news.why: Affected communities still seek access to medical studies and archives on nuclear testing.
